author: /root/api_core_docs
latest_requirement_source: Read root SpecKiwi MCP with an explicit workspaceRoot. The latest FR-ROUTE-021 AC-1 canonical integer-key order and AC-2 wildcard reference identity amendments were included.
scope: Stage 2 mounted routers, parameter hooks, and Pattern/alternative integration. General HTTP methods, later error recovery, and resource lifetime are outside this review.

findings.problem: Parameter-hook tests omit optional absence, scalar equality across different raw encodings, and canonical integer-key boundary cases.
findings.why_material: Hooks could run for absent optional captures; a cache keyed by raw capture or String identity could fail equal decoded values; numeric sorting could incorrectly classify 01 or 4294967295. Current assertions would not reliably reject those implementations.
required_controls: Register an id hook with /users{/:id}; requesting /users must respond without invoking that hook.
Match /:id/:other and then /:other/:id against /x/%78. Both id values decode to x; the hook runs once and its transformed result is restored for the second layer.
For quoted capture names 01, 4294967295, 4294967294, 2, a, assert the observed order 2, 4294967294, 01, 4294967295, a. Leading-zero names and 2^32-1 are not canonical integer indices.

findings.problem: Mount exits are inline, while the delayed parameter-hook case is root-scoped. There is no delayed child parameter callback that exits its router and restores parent request views.
findings.why_material: A held continuation can lose the child URL/base URL/query or resume the wrong router even when inline mount exits and root-level delayed hooks pass.
required_controls: Capture Next inside a child id hook without continuing. Confirm dispatch remains uncommitted and the parent after-next observer still sees the child URL/base URL.
Invoke the captured next.router later. Confirm the child route handler is skipped and the parent receives the original pathname/query with the parent base URL restored.
Assert the before/hold/after/resume/parent trace and the same Request identity. No new resource-lifetime scope is required.

findings.problem: Nested alternative registration has only positive first-match tests. Invalid parameter callback registration does not prove invalid path alternatives are atomic.
findings.why_material: Incremental registration can leave an earlier valid alternative active when a later nested malformed or null leaf fails.
required_controls: Register a valid first alternative followed by a malformed nested string. Assert rejection, then add a fallback at the first path and prove the rejected handler was never installed.
Test a null leaf according to the explicit Java SRS nullness contract.
An ambiguous precompiled Pattern may also serve as a rejected later leaf; its precise source-plus-flags form should remain valid.
findings.oracle_boundary: The pinned Express version accepts null path alternatives in this configuration. Null rejection is the explicit Java SRS registration contract, not an Express observation. A malformed nested string independently threw TypeError and did not leak the first route.

checks_passed: The recorded run contains 18 real RED failures before Stage 2 implementation; no passing behavior is claimed.
The current 2/10/a order matches the latest SRS amendment, and fresh wildcard arrays rerun hooks despite equal contents.
Mount raw text, query/original URL, root/empty/repeated/trailing separators, child options, mergeParams, numeric capture merging, and non-prefix regex skipping have concrete checks.

Router-local cache isolation, inherited undeclared names, transformed cached values, last-value recurrence, delayed hooks, cached route skip, thrown/explicit hook errors, and invalid callback registration are covered.
Advanced RegexPathPattern input and capture decoding are exercised through the public application dispatcher.
nonblocking_suggestions: Add a case-insensitive/non-strict sibling literal and an uppercase parent mount request to strengthen option locality.
Verify cached hook errors after ordered error recovery in the later error stage; the current 403 checks do not prove that future obligation.
next: Add these scoped boundary/negative cases, confirm RED, then request round 2. Maximum three rounds; stop on the first PASS.
